title: The down payment for an apartment under construction is paid on a promise
seoTitle: Down payment for apartment under construction: how much and
description: How much developers ask for apartments under construction, what you sign, and clauses that cost you. 15 percent cap, doubled refunds.
descriptionLlm: Find out what paying a down payment for an apartment under construction involves, what new laws say, and how to protect your money given to the developer.
keywords: down payment apartment under construction, pre-contract, bilateral sale purchase promise, 15 percent down payment cap, Nordis Law, new apartment payment stages
lead: At the sales office, the first thing placed in front of you is the sheet with the first serious sum: the down payment. For an apartment chosen from new apartment listings and loved from a blueprint while the building is still under work, the developer asks for 15 percent of the price from the start. You reach out, pay, sign, and that is precisely when the part few read carefully begins. Below is what binds you at that moment, where the law stops the requested sum, how money flows until handover, and through which clauses the date you receive the key can slip.

sections.h2: A pre-contract binds you to the developer from day one

blocks.x: The document signed at the down payment carries a long name, a bilateral sale purchase promise, but in discussions you hear its nicknames more often: pre-contract or preliminary contract. Such a document is not a simple reservation receipt, it is a commitment with obligations on both sides: you bind yourself to buy the apartment under the written conditions, and the developer binds to sell it to you by the deadline on the sheet.

The explanation for why developers want money ahead of time lies in site mathematics: when the residential complex is under full work, buyers' down payments become one of the sources funding construction, which is why some projects underway ask for a smaller down payment.

sections.h2: How much the developer can ask for the down payment: the 15 percent cap

blocks.x: The limit is established by Law no. 207/2025, known as the Nordis Law, and by ANCPI Order no. 1.323/2026. From the moment the developer holds the construction permit in hand, the requested down payment cannot exceed 15 percent of the apartment value. The same regulations obligate you to make two checks before any payment: the land registry of the building and the pre-apartment numbering of the unit you want.

sections.h2: The rest of the price flows in site stages

blocks.x: The usual payment structure for an apartment under construction looks like this: 15 percent at the down payment, 25 percent when the structure is finished, another 25 percent alongside installations, and the rest at handover. If you want a starting benchmark, look at apartment prices beforehand, then do the math for your project. For an apartment of 300,000 lei, for example, you put down 45,000 lei at signature, 75,000 lei when the skeleton finishes, another 75,000 lei along with pipes and wires, and leave the last 105,000 lei for key day.
You finance the largest part of the final amount, in many situations, from a mortgage loan, so you know the installment schedule before tying yourself to a monthly rate.

sections.h2: The final deadline slips through extension clauses

blocks.x: The delicate part of the down payment document lies in the deadlines chapter. The sheet can contain clauses allowing the developer to postpone signing the sale contract by 3 to 6 months without justifying anything. Well-known explanations appear on paper: the contractor fell behind with works, materials got stuck on the road, authorities delay permits and receptions. Each reason kept separately seems fine, but put together they leave you with a move-in date that shifts on its own.

If you accept such clauses without discussion, your moving plan rests in the hands of the construction site, and the period during which you pay both rent and apartment installments can drag on without anyone giving you an exact day.

sections.h2: If the sale falls through, the down payment returns with inflation and interest

blocks.x: The scenario frightening any buyer, the block left unfinished and the broken sale, has a defense line written in specialist recommendations: the sum that must return to your account starts at least from the paid down payment, updated with the inflation rate and legal interest, and at the end of the spectrum you can receive back up to double the given sum. From the 300,000 lei example, the initial 45,000 lei can return as 90,000 lei if you pursue it.
The law also touches the developer's pocket: anyone using buyers' money for other purposes risks a sanction of 1 percent of turnover, a percentage that for a large company reaches an unignorable sum.

sections.h2: You make checks before the first leu

blocks.x: The list starts with the two checks above and continues with details you ask the seller directly. You check if the document provides the mechanism by which the developer's mortgage is lifted at handover, compare the construction permit with what the seller promised you in the offer, and verify that the finishes plan is attached to the contract. You ask where your right to modify something in the apartment ends, on what verifiable benchmarks payment stages are measured, what the final handover date is, and what penalties you receive if the deadline slips. You also look for a way out of the contract for days when negotiations start poorly.
Each line on the list takes a phone call or a glance over papers, trivial time compared to what you can lose when looking at the blueprint instead of the clauses.

faq.q: How much down payment is paid for an apartment under construction?
faq.a: The legal cap stands at 15 percent of the apartment value, valid after the developer receives the construction permit. Below that, each project sets the sum in its offer.

faq.q: What happens to the money if the developer does not carry out their commitment to the end?
faq.a: You have a defense line, but you reach it only if you look for it. The sum that must return to your account starts at least from the paid down payment, updated with the inflation rate and legal interest, per specialist recommendations, and at the limit you can receive back up to double the offered sum. Taking the 300,000 lei apartment example, the initial 45,000 lei can return as 90,000 lei. In parallel, a developer caught using buyers' money for other purposes risks a sanction of 1 percent of turnover.

faq.q: Can the developer postpone signing the final contract?
faq.a: Yes, if the down payment document contains extension clauses, the deadline slips by 3 to 6 months without anyone showing you reasons. The contractor left behind with works, blocked materials, and permits sitting at authorities appear as explanations on paper, so you should read the deadlines chapter twice and negotiate a firm signing date from day one.
